If you want it, get it on sale.

review_text_raw:
I have depression. Playing games is one of a few ways I try to take my mind off of things that would typically worsen that depression, something that is proving exceptionally more difficult at the time of this writing. I actively avoid media that would obviously worsen that depression. I keep up on my anti-depression meds. This is how I take care of myself.

People are free to enjoy the media that they enjoy, and some people will, and have, really enjoyed this game. I won't fault people for that. As much as I hate to say it, I think I'm probably a case study for why some things need content warnings, because I'm going to be carrying this game's ending with me now and I really wish I didn't have to carry that on top of everything else I deal with on a day-to-day basis.

That said, I will not be directly spoiling anything. I went in blind, which if you're like me, I strongly advise you not to do. Watch a playthrough, or preferably just read up on the community posts first. Those'll mostly tell you all you need to know whether this is a game you'll be able to enjoy or not.

All that aside, the investigative gameplay was great, but a little lacking. They introduce tools and mechanics you use once and never again, which feels like a lot of wasted potential.

Again, if you're like me and prefer to play games to escape having to dwell on all the problems with real life, I advise you to give this game a pass and instead, pick up Scrutinized and play it on Detective Mode. Similar gameplay without reminding you quite as much about how much you really hate some aspects of the world you live in.

I think if I weren't in the mental state I'm in, I probably would have enjoyed the game more, and even appreciated the ending more. It is certainly realistic. It wraps up exactly how I would expect this scenario to end in the real world. I think that's why I hate it. It's just reaffirmation that good things don't actually happen to good people. Something I was already well aware of, and really didn't need a reminder.

review_text_raw:
There was a lot of effort put into this game, but I'm not quite sure if it paid off for me. The main storyline was predictable, no red herrings or distractions from this main plot. There are no consequences to any of the choices I made. Like no matter what option I picked, I was going to get the same outcome - I'd rather fail and have a rewind to try an interaction again. 

I really enjoyed some of the mechanisms that were set up - identifying cars, substances, and etc. I wish there was more of them, and a bit more substance to it rather than just clicking and having pop-ups. An example of having more substance would be if I had a car identifying task I get given a line up of cars to choose from to deduce the correct one. Or if there was a gunshot I'd have to analyse it at least a little bit, like the angle of how the shot happened could help deduce the height of the killer. But no, after I scrape the surface of a puzzle I'm pushed back into the strict dialogue. 

Some of the visuals were really silly and took me out of the immersions, [spoiler]like why was Kathrine 3ft in the hallway, and 5ft10 in the locker room[/spoiler], especially when juxtaposed to real headshots of real humans, as well as illustrations. 

As of writing this, I've completed the main storyline in 3 hours. Wasn't worth it for me.

review_text_raw: Don't get me wrong, it's an interesting story and the final plot twist is one I definitely didn't expect. The UI and the mechanics were interesting, and while it wasn't very hard at least I didn't have to ask for help so it's pretty easy access for people who aren't hardcore into mystery solving. However, I feel like this concept could have gone SO much further- the open ending could have allowed for at least twice as much story and overall I feel like the whole Operator thing should have lasted longer- either been stretched out more in time (because timeline wise this all happens VERY fast) or just... had more to do, more characters to meet? It's supposed to be a full time job and yet we practically only help with a single case a day. In short, I'll repeat what I've seen a lot of other reviews say; this game had a lot of potential. I almost feel like this could be a demo! I bought it on sale, so it's fine, but for a game that has practically only three hours of gameplay I feel like the price (while probably very justified for the developers), isn't really worth it for people with limited funds, especially since there's no real replayability. If you have the money to spare, sure, it's a fun but short game that isn't too hard, but if you want some challenge or you're trying to figure out what to spend your limited allowance on, this probably isn't it.

review_text_raw:
Has promise, but doesn't deliver.

Mechanically there are a handful of things that seem interesting and like you should pay attention to them that just don't go anywhere. There is no real point in taking notes because you are handed solutions to every problem without needing to look around or remember anything.

Cool, I can run programs from my terminal - [spoiler] e.g. I can call certain people if I pay attention to their IP addresses [/spoiler]. But does that come up at all after I'm shown it? No, it's a one-off to get my to type something into the terminal for vibes. Problems are not solveable outside of the linear storyline. Problems and solutions are presented to you side by side. There is no payoff for paying attention to details, because they don't go anywhere, you can't use them to figure anything out. Very much on rails, and a disappointing detective game experience. I almost thought this would go somewhere cool at the end [spoiler] and that you would continue the game as HAL and actually find out who the mysterious baddies are [/spoiler], but this too does not pay off. Just leaves me wanting more, but not in a good way; feels almost like a demo. When it was revealed [spoiler] who the mole was I was like yeah, ok, there are like 6 total people I have met who aren't dead, of course it's my sketchy friend Mike who's been acting weird. [/spoiler]

That being said, individual minigames and puzzles were genuinely fun to solve. I wish the game leaned more into the mechanics and systems they had, I think that is where they were strongest, and made it important and useful to take notes - reward paying attention to the details! Why give us a notepad if there's nothing you realistically need to write down? I wish I like this game more!

I dunno if they were going for dark and edgy or if they wanted something that would happen in real life, but either way I play games for the illusion that good guys can win. (I don't count HAL as a good guy because she manipulates everyone for her own ends)  While not as bad of an ending as say, Jessika, it's still leaving me with the same kind of hollow "why did I even bother?" type feeling.

This is going to be the oddest negative review I have ever left. This game got me philosophical about reviews: Is a game review to describe whether I think the game is well made? Or is the game review to describe whether I enjoyed it? It's so rare that these two things are out of alignment, I wasn't sure what to write here. I have decided to write a review based on my enjoyment.

So let me just say: This game is well made. It is VERY well made. It's mechanics are a little bit "Papers, Please", a little bit "Clandestine", and a little bit "The Roottrees are Dead" - all meant as a compliment. The production values are top notch. And the story is very well written and very engaging.

And that's where the problem comes in. When a game is this good, my enjoyment hinges on the story being satisfying - and this story is FAR from satisfying. The ending is a cliffhanger that should have been the INTRODUCTION to a game, not a game in itself. And aside from being an incomplete story, the ending is nothing but [spoiler]bad things happening to good people and bad people getting away with it[/spoiler]. And I find that an extremely unsatisfying experience.

So I leave this review to convey an experience for people like me: people who can appreciate a masterfully crafted game that delivers a deeply unsatisfying story. If I'd known how the story ended, I wouldn't have bothered.

I wish I liked this more. This is not a game about being an FBI operator, solving cases with little guidance. This is a standard conspiracy game that pretends to have options when it is all very railroaded. The game is:
5% cool deductive work, 
70% listening to people re-explain what is happening in case you quit and reloaded the game after each day
25% watching a black screen and listening to someone walking home

I like the controls, as simple as they are. But I am shocked to see people compare this to anything like Obra Dinn or Case of the Golden Idol. If you have are ok with a corny story, lots of reading and listening (not detective work, just fluff), and one of the worst time-sensitive, feel-bad, mini games if seen in a game like this, then you might actually enjoy your time. This is a $5 game on sale if you have exhausted the other detective games on Steam.
